resale_co.name: Certificate of Land/Structure Compliance (resale inspection; posted as 'Application Certificate of Occupancy')
resale_co.issued_by: Construction Official, Construction, Zoning and Code Enforcement Office (Dept. of Construction Enforcement)
requirements: Walks and driveways free of trip hazards
Yard free of weeds and debris, grass cut
House number at least 4 inches high, visible from the street
Paint not peeling or cracking, no untreated wood exposed
Service entry cable, gutters, downspouts, decks, steps and building exterior (foundation, walls, roof, glazing, basement hatch) in good condition; 3 or more risers need a graspable rail
Floor coverings without trip hazards; walls and ceilings in good condition
Smoke alarm within 10 feet of bedrooms and on every level including the basement; CO alarm within 10 feet of all sleeping rooms
Fire extinguisher 2A:10B:C, 10 lb maximum, mounted in the kitchen, visible and readily accessible, top no more than 5 feet above the floor (form still lists it)
Graspable rails on all stairs including the basement
Bathrooms have an operable window or a fan exhausting outside
GFCI protection on outlets within 6 feet of a sink and in the garage, basement and outside
A light fixture in every hallway, interior stairway, bathroom, kitchen, laundry room, boiler or furnace room and basement
Plumbing fixtures working with hot and cold water and no visible leaks; water heater relief valve discharge within 6 inches of the floor
Gas appliances vented with combustion air and clearances; dryer vented outside with metal flex duct; washer drains to the drain system
Door locks meet code (no double keyed locks); at least one insect screen in every room

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Land/Structure Compliance Application (posted as 'Application Certificate of Occupancy' on the Construction, Zoning & Code Enforcement page) with the property use, occupancy, lockbox code, seller, agent, buyer, settlement date and whether the home will be rented, and submit it with the fee to the Construction Office (the form lists City Hall, 1 W. New Jersey Avenue; the web page lists 741 Shore Road), 9:00 am to 5:00 pm weekdays. The office-use section takes cash or check and records any open permits.

resale_co.notes: City Code Chapter 169, Article IV (read in full on ecode360) requires the Construction Official to inspect any single-family home, condominium unit or building of four or fewer units upon its conveyance or a contract to convey it, and to issue a certificate of land/structure compliance after a satisfactory inspection; the fee is set by resolution. The City's application form (updated 4/14/23) charges $250.00 per dwelling unit and $100.00 per reinspection, and its checklist is titled 'Requirements for all resale and rental inspections'. Page 2 of the same scanned form carries an older notice (effective 6/14/2007) of a $15 reinspection appointment fee when smoke/CO alarms or the extinguisher fail; the current $100 reinspection fee on page 1 may supersede it. The form still lists a kitchen fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the state sale certificate in February 2025; the City's own inspection checklist may still require it. The form's footer address (City Hall, 1 W. New Jersey Avenue, 609-927-9088 ext. 142) differs from the web page's Construction Office address (741 Shore Road). Other office staff: Roe Howell, Technical Assistant to the Construction Official, (609) 927-9088 ext. 148, rhowell@spgov.org. The form also asks whether the home will be a short-term (under 175 days) or long-term rental; rental licensing (Ch. 169, Art. V) is a separate program. The Code also calls for the same inspection on a refinance when a lender asks (§169-43).

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level and outside each separate sleeping area, per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 (battery-only alarms must be 10-year sealed units)
Carbon monoxide alarm in the immediate vicinity of the sleeping areas (homes with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)

The City's resale inspection form (2023) also checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and a 2A:10B:C extinguisher of 10 lb or less mounted to the kitchen wall, and notes 10-year sealed lithium battery smoke alarms have been required since 1/1/2019 (existing hardwired alarms excepted)

fire_cert.notes: The City says it no longer has a Bureau of Fire Prevention and that the service is provided by the State, the July 2026 LEA registry lists Somers Point as State enforced (S), and the state fire directory lists 'NJ Division of Fire Safety' for smoke detector compliance in Somers Point. However, the DCA's July 17, 2026 list of State-enforced towns still shows Somers Point without the 'SC' (smoke certs) flag that it gives Port Republic and Weymouth, so confirm the DCA online certificate is the right one here; confidence is medium. State fees ($45 / $90 / $161) are cited from the N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) adoption in the NJ Register. The City's own Land/Structure Compliance inspection also checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and the extinguisher. The directory gives (609) 633-6132 for Louis Kilmer; the Bureau's own page gives (609) 633-6106, which is used here.

open_questions: Who issues the smoke/CO certificate for a Somers Point sale: the NJ DCA online portal (the City says the State provides fire inspection service), or is the City's own resale inspection enough? DCA's 7/17/2026 list does not mark Somers Point 'SC'.
Lead time before closing and how long the Land/Structure Compliance certificate stays valid are not stated.
Whether the 2007 $15 smoke/CO reinspection fee on page 2 of the form still applies alongside the $100 reinspection fee, and whether the City still requires the fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19.
